html:
A railway about 415 kilometres long, built by the Japanese army in 1942 and 1943 from Ban Pong in Thailand to Thanbyuzayat in Burma, to supply its forces in the Burma campaign. It is remembered as the Death Railway.

The sea route around Malaya was open to Allied submarines, so Japan wanted a land link from Bangkok to Rangoon. The line was pushed through jungle and mountains in about a year. It was built by roughly 60,000 Allied prisoners of war, British, Australian, Dutch and American, and by far more Asian labourers, Burmese, Malay, Tamil, Chinese and Javanese, many brought by force or false promises.

They worked with hand tools, with little food, under beatings, through cholera and monsoon rains. About 12,000 prisoners died, and by most estimates over 90,000 Asian labourers.

The bridge over the Khwae Yai river at Kanchanaburi became famous through the 1957 film The Bridge on the River Kwai. Part of the line still runs in Thailand. It is one of the great crimes of the Second World War in Asia.
